text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool 'hotpath-eu' at 98% utilization, queue length rising (1200). Spike in 429s observed across prod routes. Autoscaler attempted scale_up but failures reported. Paging oncall.

oncall-bot: @sre-jen you're currently on-call (policy: primary-sre).

sre-jen: I'm taking it. investigating autoscaler + rate limiter. attaching first-pass checks.

infra-miguel: Autoscaler logs show repeated failures: 
```
autoscaler: scale_up attempt=3 -> failed reason=MaxPoolCapacityReached limit=10
```
We hit the reserved account GPU cap (10).

eng-ash: Also saw a config change ~2h ago to ratecap: prod tier tokens went from 1000 -> 100 in the last rollout. Could explain sudden 429s when queueing increased.

sre-jen: Searching rate_limiter logs... found a flood of denies: `rate_limiter: deny request tier=prod token_available=0 src=svc-canary`. Looks like canary health checks are tagged as prod and draining tokens.

support-tom: Customer 42 reported 40% error rate starting ~10:34 UTC, escalation open.

product-kate: Do we have an emergency fallback to a lower-cost pool or smaller model to restore customer experience?

eng-ash: Proposed mitigations (order):
1) Temporarily increase prod tier tokens to 500 via KV to stop hard 429s.
2) Patch health-check tagging so canary traffic is classified as internal (not prod).
3) Reassign idle GPUs from non-critical dedicated pools to hotpath pool.
4) If quota allows, request cloud GPU quota bump to increase autoscaler max.
5) Enable CPU fallback for non-low-latency routes as last resort.

sre-jen: Doing step 1 now: patching `config/ratepolicy/prod.tokens` -> 500.

sre-jen: Patch applied. Observing metrics... queue: 1200 -> 480 within 90s. 429s dropping.

infra-miguel: Kicked spare GPUs from dev-reserved pool into hotpath. This is ephemeral until quota sorted.

eng-ash: Health-check tagging fix merged to canary: `svc=internal` now set for probe requests. Will deploy in 30s.

sre-jen: After tagging fix deployed, saw additional drop to queue 180 and 429s near baseline. Latency back to normal for most routes.

support-tom: Confirmed customer 42 error rate back down, they acknowledged the recovery.

product-kate: Good. We should notify impacted customers and schedule postmortem. Any data on how long tokens were low?

eng-ash: Change was rolled ~2h before spike. Impact window ~10:30-10:38 UTC. Root cause appears to be twofold: conservative prod token change + mis-tagged canary health checks amplifying consumption. Autoscaler hitting account max made it worse.

sre-jen: Creating incident record and collecting logs. severity=sev2. Moving to #incidents-postmortem for full writeup. For immediate next steps: revert prod token to 1000 in staging, create guard in rollout pipeline to prevent tier token drops >50% without signoff, add a rate-limiter metric to alert on external vs internal token usage.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-315. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-saturation>.

sre-jen: Thanks team. I'll hand off to postmortem owners in 10m.
